root_cause.text: The previous fix (commit d6d2b0e1538d) conditionally skipped page pool cleanup when a skb was present, causing page_pool fragments allocated for non-linear skb buffers to leak when errors occur during subsequent buffer processing before those fragments are linked to the skb.
root_cause.evidence: The patch shows that the conditional logic `} else { page_pool_put_full_page(...) }` was removed and replaced with unconditional `page_pool_put_full_page(q->page_pool, page, true);` execution. The CVE description explicitly states: "If an error occurs on the subsequents buffers belonging to the non-linear part of the skb...the page_pool fragment will not be linked to the skb so it will not return to the pool in the airoha_qdma_rx_process() error path." The fix ensures that regardless of whether a skb exists, the page is always returned to the pool on error, preventing the leak of unlinked fragments.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch shows that the original code had an `else` clause that only called `page_pool_put_full_page()` when `q->skb` was NULL. This meant that when an error occurred on subsequent buffers of a non-linear skb (where `q->skb` is not NULL), the page fragment would not be returned to the pool. The fix removes the conditional logic and unconditionally calls `page_pool_put_full_page()` for all error paths, ensuring page fragments are always properly recycled regardless of whether they were linked to the skb or not.

Do not recycle the page twice in airoha_qdma_rx_process rou
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit d6d2b0e1538d5c381ec0ca95afaf772c096ea5dc
Author: Lorenzo Bianconi <lorenzo@kernel.org>
Date:   Thu May 15 08:33:06 2025 +0200

    net: airoha: Fix page recycling in airoha_qdma_rx_process()
    
    Do not recycle the page twice in airoha_qdma_rx_process routine in case
    of error. Just run dev_kfree_skb() if the skb has been allocated and marked
    for recycling. Run page_pool_put_full_page() directly if the skb has not
    been allocated yet.
    Moreover, rely on DMA address from q
bic_trace_step.reason: The commit introduces a conditional cleanup in the free_frag error path (lines 697-702). The new logic only calls page_pool_put_full_page() when q->skb is NULL (else branch). However, this is insufficient to prevent the vulnerability described: when page_pool fragments are allocated for non-linear skb buffers and errors occur during subsequent buffer processing BEFORE those fragments are linked to the skb, the fragments will still leak. The problem is that the code unconditionally allocates page_pool pages earlier in the function (not shown in diff context), but the error handling at free_frag only recycles the page if q->skb is NULL. If a page was allocated and added to the skb's frags array before the error occurs, but q->skb itself is still set, the conditional logic will skip page_pool_put_full_page() and instead call dev_kfree_skb(), which may not properly return all allocated fragments to the page pool. The fix is incomplete because it doesn't account for fragments that may have already been attached to q->skb before the error condition is detected.

commit e12182ddb6e712951d21a50e2c8ccd700e41a40c
Author: Lorenzo Bianconi <lorenzo@kernel.org>
Date:   Tue Mar 4 15:21:09 2025 +0100

    net: airoha: Enable Rx Scatter-Gather
    
    EN7581 SoC can receive 9k frames. Enable the reception of Scatter-Gather
    (SG) frames.
    
    Signed-off-by: Lorenzo Bianconi <lorenzo@kernel.org>
    Reviewed-by: Simon Horman <horms@kernel.org>
    Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20250304-airoha-eth-rx-sg-v1-2-283ebc61120e@kernel.org
    Signed-off-by: Jakub
bic_trace_step.reason:
This commit introduces Scatter-Gather (SG) frame support by modifying the Rx processing logic to handle multi-buffer frames. The vulnerability root cause describes a page pool cleanup issue where fragments allocated for non-linear skb buffers leak when errors occur during buffer processing before fragments are linked to the skb.

The commit shows the problematic pattern: (1) It allocates page pool buffers via napi_build_skb() and skb_add_rx_frag() for SG frames, (2) It introduces a goto free_frag label that attempts cleanup with 'page_pool_put_full_page(q->page_pool, page, true); dev_kfree_skb(q->skb); q->skb = NULL;', but (3) The cleanup logic is insufficient because when errors occur during intermediate buffer processing (before all fragments are linked), previously allocated fragments in q->skb remain referenced by the skb but the page pool cleanup only handles the current page. The skb itself may be partially constructed with fragments that won't be properly reclaimed if an error occurs mid-SG-frame processing. The fix would require unconditional page pool cleanup for all fragments regardless of skb state, but this commit does not implement that - it only cleans up the current page and attempts to free the skb, which doesn't address the core issue of leaked fragments from previous iterations when errors occur during SG frame assembly.

bic_trace_step.reason: This commit introduces the vulnerable construct described in the root cause. The code now uses scatter-gather (SG) frame handling with `q->skb` to accumulate multiple buffer fragments. The vulnerability exists because: (1) When processing the first buffer fragment, `q->skb = napi_build_skb(e->buf, q->buf_size)` is called at line 651. (2) For subsequent fragments in a scattered frame, `skb_add_rx_frag()` is called at line 663-665 to add page fragments to the skb. (3) However, if an error occurs after fragments are allocated/added but before the frame is complete (before `QDMA_DESC_MORE_MASK` check at line 668 indicates the last fragment), the `free_frag` label at line 705 only calls `page_pool_put_full_page(q->page_pool, page, true)` for the current fragment and `dev_kfree_skb(q->skb)` for the skb. (4) The critical issue: when `dev_kfree_skb(q->skb)` is called, it will free the skb but the page pool fragments that were already added via `skb_add_rx_frag()` in previous iterations are NOT properly returned to the page pool - they are only freed when the skb is destroyed, but the page_pool reference counting may not be correct for fragments added mid-stream. The code lacks proper cleanup of intermediate fragments that were added to `q->skb` before an error occurs, which is exactly the vulnerability described: 'page_pool fragments allocated for non-linear skb buffers to leak when errors occur during subsequent buffer processing before those fragments are linked to the skb.'
